header.running_head: Weeping Over the Deaths of Elders

blocks.text: Hadhrat Thumaamah (RA), Hadhrat Zaid (RA), Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Humayd (RA) Weep at the Death of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA)

Hadhrat Abul Ash'ath San'aani says, "The governor of San'aa was a Sahabi called Thumaamah bin Adi (RA). When he heard of the death of Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA), he wept and said, 'Khilaafah on the pattern of Nubuwwah has been snatched away and it shall now be kingship and tyranny. Whoever has power over something will now devour it.'"[^2]
Hadhrat Zaid bin Ali narrates that Hadhrat Zaid bin Thaabit (RA) wept over Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) the day he was martyred in his home.

Hadhrat Abu Saalih reports, "Hadhrat Abu Hurayrah (RA) wept whenever someone mentioned what had happened to Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA). It is as if I can actually hear him say, 'Ah! Ah!' as he wept uncontrollably."

Hadhrat Yahya bin Sa'eed reports that when Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was martyred, Hadhrat Abu Humayd Saa'idi (RA) who was a veteran of the Battle of Badr vowed never to carry out certain actions and never to laugh until the day he meets Allaah.[^3]
Finding a Change in Oneself at the Death of an Elder
The Statements of Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA), Hadhrat Ubay (RA) and Hadhrat Anas (RA) about the Changes within themselves after the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ
Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) once said, "We had hardly left from burying Rasulullaah ﷺ when we found a change within our hearts."[^4]

Hadhrat Ubay bin Ka'b (RA) said, "When with Rasulullaah ﷺ, we were united but no sooner did he leave us and we divided left and right." Another narration states that he said, "We all looked in the same direction when we were with Rasulullaah ﷺ but when he passed away, we started looking this way and that."[^5]
Hadhrat Anas bin Maalik (RA) said, "The day Rasulullaah ﷺ passed away, everything in Madinah became dark. We had hardly finished burying Rasulullaah
